title: How a Member's Utilization Management Program Follows the Plan Enrollment
content:
**Rule.** The Utilization Management Program review program follows the plan enrollment: it opens with it, takes effect on its effective date, ends with it and is restored by a COBRA reinstatement; member services never opens or ends it on request. A sponsor's change of package takes effect at plan year renewal, and the new package's requirements apply to claims from that date, subject to approvals carried over. Electronic requests are accepted when the package accepts electronic prior authorization, urgent reviews are taken around the clock when the package provides round-the-clock urgent intake, criteria follow the package's clinical criteria source, and when the package's denial notices include alternatives a denial lists the formulary alternatives that need no review.

## Status of the program

| Event | Program status before | Program status after |
|---|---|---|
| Plan enrollment created | — | pending effective |
| Plan coverage effective date reached | pending effective | active |
| Future-dated plan enrollment cancelled before it takes effect | pending effective | terminated |
| Plan coverage ends | active | terminated |
| COBRA reinstatement | terminated | active |
| Sponsor moves its members to another package (normally at plan year renewal) | active | active, under the new package |

All of these changes come from the plan enrollment and the sponsor; none is made by member services at a caller's request.

### Questions the rule answers

**A member asks member services to close their review program. Is that done?** No. The program ends only with the plan enrollment.

**The sponsor moves from Northbridge Clinical Standard to Northbridge Clinical Advanced at plan year renewal. Which requirements apply to a claim after that date?** Those of Northbridge Clinical Advanced, subject to the approvals carried over.
